subject: biology
title: Cholera and controlling the spread of disease
key_idea: Clean water, hygienic food, good personal hygiene, waste disposal and sewage treatment stop pathogens spreading. (Supplement) Cholera is a bacterial disease spread in contaminated water. Its toxin makes the gut lining secrete chloride ions, so water leaves the blood by osmosis.

blocks.text: Many pathogens spread through water, food and waste. This section covers five ways to break that chain.

rows: Water is treated so that it has no pathogens in it. People then cannot drink pathogens and become infected.
Washing hands, cleaning surfaces, cooking food thoroughly and keeping raw and cooked food apart stop pathogens reaching food and multiplying in it.
Washing hands after using the toilet and before eating stops pathogens passing from person to person or onto food.
Rubbish and waste are removed and stored safely. Pests such as flies and rats cannot feed and breed in it and carry pathogens to people or food.
Human waste contains pathogens. Treating it stops them reaching rivers, drinking water and food crops.

blocks.text: The details of the stages of sewage treatment are not needed.

items: Pathogens spread through water, food, waste and touch.
Clean water, hygienic food preparation, personal hygiene, waste disposal and sewage treatment each break the chain of infection.

blocks.text: (Supplement) Cholera is a good example of a disease that spreads when water or sewage is not controlled.

items: The bacteria are transmitted in **contaminated water**.
A person becomes infected by drinking water that contains the bacteria.
Water becomes contaminated when sewage gets into it. This is why clean water and sewage treatment prevent cholera.
Cholera is caused by a bacterium.
It is spread by drinking contaminated water, so clean water and sewage treatment prevent it.

sections.heading: How the cholera toxin causes diarrhoea

blocks.text: (Supplement) The bacteria live in the small intestine and make a toxin. The toxin does the damage by changing how water moves.

items.meaning: A poison produced by a pathogen.
The space inside the small intestine.
The tendency of water to move. The more dissolved ions in a solution, the lower its water potential.

diagram.alt: A sequencing activity. Six events are put in order, from the cholera bacteria producing a toxin to diarrhoea causing dehydration and loss of ions.
diagram.prompt: Put these events in the order that causes diarrhoea.
steps: Cells lining the small intestine secrete chloride ions.
Chloride ions move into the lumen of the small intestine.
The water potential of the fluid in the small intestine becomes lower.
Water moves from the blood into the small intestine by osmosis.
Watery diarrhoea causes dehydration and loss of ions from the blood.

items: Water moves by **osmosis**, from the higher water potential in the blood to the lower water potential in the gut.
The extra water makes the faeces watery. This is **diarrhoea**.
The body loses a lot of water, so the person becomes dehydrated.
Ions are lost from the blood along with the water.
The toxin causes chloride ions to be secreted into the small intestine.
This lowers the water potential in the gut, so water leaves the blood by osmosis.
The result is diarrhoea, dehydration and loss of ions.

checks.q: Name two ways of controlling the spread of disease through water.
checks.a: Any two from: a clean (treated) water supply, sewage treatment, safe disposal of waste.

checks.q: (Supplement) State the type of pathogen that causes cholera and how it is spread.
checks.a: A bacterium. It is spread in contaminated water that people drink.

checks.q: (Supplement) Explain how the cholera toxin causes diarrhoea.
checks.a: The toxin makes cells secrete chloride ions into the small intestine. This lowers the water potential there, so water moves in from the blood by osmosis. The faeces become watery.

worked_example.question:
People with cholera can become very dehydrated.

Explain how cholera causes dehydration.
answer_points: The cholera bacterium produces a toxin.
The toxin causes secretion of chloride ions into the small intestine.
The ions lower the water potential in the gut, so water moves out of the cells and blood.
Water moves down the water potential gradient, from high to low water potential, by osmosis.
This causes diarrhoea and a loss of water from the body.
worked_example.tip: Any four score one mark each. Link the chloride ions to water potential and osmosis.
